title: Colorado limits gas lawn equipment for Front Range companies
h1: Colorado regulators voted to limit summer use of gas-powered lawn equipment by Front Range landscaping companies, starting in 2027
description: Colorado's Air Quality Control Commission voted November 20, 2026 to limit summer use of gas lawn equipment by Front Range companies, starting at 85% in 2027.
standfirst: The rule applies from June 1 to August 31 and tightens through 2032. People who do their own yard work are not covered.
keywords: Colorado gas lawn equipment rule, Air Quality Control Commission, Front Range ozone, commercial landscapers Colorado, electric lawn equipment, ozone 2027
takeaways: The Air Quality Control Commission approved the rule unanimously on November 20, 2026.
From June 1 to August 31, companies may use 85% of their gas equipment in 2027, falling to 10% in 2032.
Homeowners doing their own yard work and the largest ride-on mowers are not covered.
body: Landscaping companies on Colorado's northern Front Range will have to idle part of their gas-powered equipment each summer starting in 2027. The state Air Quality Control Commission approved the rule unanimously on Friday, November 20, The Colorado Sun reported. It expands limits that until now applied only to government agencies, according to Colorado Public Radio.

The limits run from June 1 to August 31 in nine northern Front Range counties, the Sun reported. Commercial operators must file an inventory of their equipment with the state. In 2027 they may use 85% of their gas-powered machines during those months. The share falls to 65% in 2028, 25% in 2030 and 10% in 2032.

The rule covers string trimmers, hedge trimmers, blowers, edgers, pole saws and push or walk-behind mowers. People who do their own yard work do not have to comply, the state health department said in a statement cited by the Sun. The largest ride-on mowers were left out because commercial operators have fewer affordable electric options.

Sensors recorded ozone violations on 66 days along the Front Range this past summer, one short of the record of 67, according to the Sun. The region has missed federal ozone standards for 14 straight years, CPR reported. State health officials say lawn and garden equipment accounts for about 13% of ground-level ozone pollution in the area that fails those standards.

The state Air Pollution Control Division found that electric equipment costs about the same as gas models and is sometimes cheaper, CPR reported. Batteries, chargers and electrical panel work could add between $275 and several thousand dollars. Groups representing landscapers and equipment makers generally opposed the rule because of cost.

Colorado offers a 30% tax credit on some electric lawn equipment until 2030, according to CPR, and the Regional Air Quality Council offers grants to commercial operators, the Sun reported. "Instead of thousands of dollars, we need millions of dollars," the council's executive director, Michael Silverstein, told CPR.
The first summer limit begins on June 1, 2027. Operators should check the state's requirements and available incentives before buying replacement equipment.

faq.q: Does Colorado's gas lawn equipment rule apply to homeowners?
faq.a: No. The state health department said people who do their own yard work are not expected to comply, The Colorado Sun reported.

faq.q: When do the limits on commercial gas lawn equipment start?
faq.a: In summer 2027. From June 1 to August 31, commercial operators may use 85% of their gas-powered equipment, a share that falls to 10% in 2032.
